A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a non-[[Definition:Trivial Group|trivial]] finite [[Definition:P-Group|$p$-group]].
Then its [[Definition:Center of Group|center]] $\map Z G$ is non-trivial.

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ represent the non-central conjugacy classes.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \order G = \order {\map Z G} + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \index G {\map {C_G} {x_i} }$

substitutions.the indices: proper divisors of p^n greater than 1

derived.divisibility of each term: p divides the order of the center

object_map.reformulation: Read the class equation modulo p.

validity_conditions: Each centralizer of a non-central element is a proper subgroup, so its index is a non-trivial power of p.
The center always contains the identity, so its order is at least 1.
proof_plan:
For each non-central $x_i$, $\map {C_G} {x_i}$ is a proper subgroup.
By [[Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)|Lagrange's Theorem]], $\index G {\map {C_G} {x_i} }$ divides $p^n$ and exceeds $1$, so $p$ divides it.

By the [[Class Equation]]:
:$\displaystyle \order {\map Z G} = p^n - \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \index G {\map {C_G} {x_i} } \equiv 0 \pmod p$

As $e \in \map Z G$, $\order {\map Z G} \ge 1$, hence $\order {\map Z G} \ge p$.
{{qed}}
